best_for: Medical students, language learners and anyone memorizing a lot of facts who want flashcards scheduled for them, free on the desktop.

points.title: Reviews at the right moment
points.text: Anki asks you to recall an answer, then schedules the card again just before you would forget it. Easy cards come back less often. You can use the classic SM-2 scheduler or the newer FSRS.

points.title: Free on the desktop
points.text: The Windows, Mac and Linux apps are free and open source under the AGPL 3.0. AnkiWeb sync between devices is also free.

points.title: Phones differ
points.text: AnkiDroid on Android is free and run by volunteers. AnkiMobile on iPhone and iPad is a paid app, and its sales fund Anki's development.

points.title: Add-ons extend it
points.text: Shared add-ons on AnkiWeb add features to the desktop app.

points.title: Arm builds everywhere
points.text: Windows needs 10 or later on x64, with a build for Windows 11 on Arm. The Mac app needs macOS 13 and has Intel and Apple silicon builds.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is verified
points.text: On Flathub the Anki Flatpak is verified and published by Damien Elmes, Anki's developer, for x64 and Arm64. The project also offers Linux tarballs.

points.title: Older versions on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 47 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
